items.title: Better scores do not always mean better perceived sound
items.summary: Optimising several learned mean-opinion-score predictors raised their scores, but a MUSHRA listening test found no improvement in perceived speech quality. It is a timely reminder that human listening must remain part of acoustic-system evaluation.

items.title: Neural operators for faster metamaterial simulations
items.summary: Wavelet-encoded Fourier neural operators learned multiple elastic-wave eigenmodes across metamaterial geometries. The authors report that the trained model greatly accelerated the simulation stage relative to finite-element analysis, pointing to new possibilities for design exploration.

items.title: Designing sound installations around acoustic niches
items.summary: A laboratory study of a proposed Paris sound installation found that its perceptual effect depended strongly on the time context. Reactive composition strategies may therefore need to differ between traffic-dominated and quieter conditions.

items.title: KTH upgrades its sound and vibration laboratory
items.summary: KTH is modernising the Marcus Wallenberg Laboratory with a modular anechoic chamber and a larger reverberation room, expanding capacity for absorption, transmission, sound-generation, and noise-control measurements.
